title: Pick This Wrong and You Could Blow Your Deal
description:
What’s the difference between SDE (Seller’s Discretionary Earnings) and EBITDA—and why does it matter when you’re buying a business?

Think of it like pruning a peach tree (yes, really). There should be enough gaps to throw a chicken through… and when you’re evaluating an accounting firm, you need to know which “gaps” in the numbers actually matter to you as the buyer.

In this video, I break down:
✔️ When to use SDE vs EBITDA in small business deals
✔️ Why owner-operators should care about SDE
✔️ Why investors and absentee owners focus on EBITDA
✔️ The tricky math when multiple partners are involved
✔️ How to figure out what you’ll actually take home as the new owner

If you’re buying (or selling) an accounting firm—or any small business—you need to understand these metrics before you sign an LOI.
